en: Canyon trail - watch your step at dusk!
No quests yet - explore the canyon!
Gather 4 wood logs to light the campfire.
Craft a stone axe (2 stones and 1 log) from the journal.
Craft a hunting bow (3 logs) from the journal.
Build a shelter (8 logs and 4 stones) to get through the night.
Press M or the Close button
Walk to choose the spot (green = valid) then place it.
Ground too steep to build here.
Too many structures in the canyon.
What a nap! Stamina restored. Wake-up point saved.
You're not sleepy: wait for night.
You sleep until dawn. Stamina restored. Wake-up point saved.
Hit! Walk up to butcher the animal.
Shoot a deer with your bow then butcher it to gather raw meat.
Cook raw meat on a full campfire.
The spring needs time to refill...
You need an equipped axe to chop this tree.
You need an equipped sickle to pick these berries.
Out of arrows! Craft some from the journal.
Axe equipped: get close to a tree and act to chop it.
Sickle equipped: get close to a berry bush to pick the berries.
Bow equipped: hold Shoot to draw, release to fire. Game near the crosshair is locked on.
Equip the axe (tool bar) and fell 3 trees: get close and act several times.
Craft a sickle from the journal (level 2 required).
Equip the sickle and pick 6 berries from the red bushes.
You need an equipped hoe to work the soil.
You need seeds (pick berries to find some).
Seed sown: the harvest will be ready in a few minutes.
You need an equipped sickle to shear.
Hoe equipped: get close to a placed plot to sow your seeds.
Craft a hoe from the journal (level 3 required).
Craft a farm plot and place it from the bag (Bag tab, Place button).
Equip the hoe, sow seeds on the plot, wait for them to grow and harvest 4 vegetables.
Feed a chicken, sheep, cow or goat (vegetables, berries or seeds) until it is tamed.
Collect milk, wool (with the sickle) or eggs 3 times from your tamed animals.
Offer meat to a stray dog until it is tamed (level 3 required). It follows you and improves your hunting.
Tame a horse with vegetables or berries (level 5 required), then ride it.
Watering can equipped: water a growing crop to speed it up.
The soil drinks it in: growth speeds up.
Prepare 3 dishes at the campfire: meat, eggs, vegetables, bread (2 wheat) or soup (milk and vegetables).
Craft a watering can (level 4), equip it and water 2 growing crops.
Sow grain seeds (sometimes found when harvesting vegetables) and harvest wheat.
Shear sheep with the sickle and craft a wool bed (level 4): it lets you sleep at night.
Craft a pen (level 4) and place it: tamed livestock nearby moves in and produces faster.
It starts to rain: your crops are watered.
Watch two seasons go by (6 game days each). Crops grow slower in winter and thirst is sharper in summer; rain waters your plots.
%s has spotted you! Use the bow or the axe (or get close to a fire).
%s is down. You collect pelts and meat.
%s was frightened by a prowler: its production is delayed. A pen would protect it.
You passed out: you come to at the starting camp.
Coyotes (from level 2) and wolves (from level 4) prowl at night. Equip the bow or the axe (attack button) and take one down; a well-fed campfire keeps them away.
Craft a cloak from 3 pelts and 1 wool (level 3): it reduces damage taken by 35% and keeps you warm (+7 °C) on autumn and winter nights.
Howling… a wolf pack is prowling nearby!
The sky darkens at once: a storm breaks out!
the map reveals further (+20 % per level)
hunger and thirst drain slower (−8 % per level)
Howdy, stranger. I'm the old trapper — I know every trail in this canyon.
Wolves prowl at night, and deer pelts sell well at the old ford.
Bring me 3 pelts and I'll gear you up for it.
Talk to the trapper near the start and accept his quest: bring him 3 pelts.
Craft a campfire (level 2) and place it from the bag: it burns wood, cooks your dishes and keeps prowlers away.
Craft a chest (level 3) and place it at camp: it stores your resources, except tools and arrows.
This place has not been discovered yet.
Level 3 is required to travel fast.
Too hungry or thirsty to travel.
Discover 3 sites (ruins, caves) by walking up to them: the map reveals itself and fast travel opens (level 3).
Open 2 treasure chests in ruins and caves: each holds an ancient relic.
The line is in the water… be patient.
Craft a fishing rod (level 2), walk up to a pond, cast and strike as soon as it bites: catch 3 fish. Dawn, dusk and rain make them bite faster.
Offer a relic at the altar near the starting signpost: each offering grants a permanent blessing.
You need an ancient relic (chests in ruins and caves).
The altar is fulfilled: all three blessings are yours.
She gives milk: come back to milk her.
She gives milk: come back to milk her.
It gives wool, sheared with the sickle.
She lays eggs for you to collect.
It follows you and helps with hunting.
You walked away: the line is lost.
From the starting signpost, walk due south (bearing 180°, about fifty metres) to the river. You can drink anywhere along it.
Open the map, tap a spot, then “Place a marker”. The compass then shows its heading, and the map its bearing and distance.
From the starting signpost, follow bearing 305° (north-west) for about 170 m to the heart of the pinewood, where the trees close in.
From the starting signpost, bearing 150° (south-east), about 150 m: cross the river and climb onto the Red Mesas plateau. Look for the ramp, the cliffs cannot be climbed.
Follow the river west, upstream, to the lake it flows from (bearing 260° from the start, over 200 m).
Eight markers at most: remove one first.
You are getting cold: stand near a lit fire or a shelter, or wear a fur cloak. Being wet chills you faster.
Take a close look at what you come across: it is noted automatically. %d / %d observations.
Take a close look at animals, plants and landscapes: each one goes into the Notebook (Journal). Make 8 observations.
Grazes at the edge of the woods and bolts at the slightest sound.
A large, wary grazer of the plains.
Hops between bushes; its long ears give it away.
Small and quick, it hides in the grass.
Prowls at dusk. A well-fed fire keeps it away.
An evening hunter, wary yet bold.
Stronger and more stubborn than the coyote: avoid it at night.
It only shows itself to seasoned travellers.
Gives milk once fed and tamed.
Its wool makes beds and cloaks.
A farm animal with a thick fleece.
Lays eggs every day once tamed.
Once tamed, it carries you much faster.
Bites best at dawn, dusk and in the rain.
You need a fishing rod to meet it.
The wood of the pinewood: chop it with an axe.
Grows in numbers in the north-west of the canyon.
Stores water in its stems; its spines sting.
A rosette of fleshy leaves that flowers only once.
A small bush that holds the sand.
A modest bush, all over the canyon.
They colour the riverbanks in spring.
Its berries ease hunger; they grow back.
A nourishing bush, often near water.
A sandstone column carved by wind and rain.
An odd rock column, on the mesas.
Erosion wore through the rock until it opened.
A pierced rock, rare and striking.
What is left of an old plateau, isolated by erosion.
It winds from one lake to the other; you can wade across.
South of the start, you can hear water.
Hills covered in pines, cool and shady.
To the north-west, where the trees close in.
From up here you can see the whole canyon.
Climb the mesas to the south-east.
You are ready. Follow the goals at the top of the screen, and enjoy exploring!
Place your left thumb anywhere on the left half of the screen and drag to [b]walk[/b].
[b]Walk[/b] with W A S D (or Z Q S D). Hold Shift to run.
Drag your right thumb across the screen to [b]look around[/b].
Walk up to a stone or a branch on the ground and tap the [b]target[/b] button that appears on the right to pick it up.
Walk up to a stone or a branch on the ground and press [b]E[/b] to pick it up.
Open the [b]Journal[/b] (button at the bottom): quests, crafting, belongings, notebook and settings.
Open the [b]Journal[/b] with the C key: quests, crafting, belongings, notebook and settings.
Tap the [b]minimap[/b] at the top right to open the map. Tap a spot to place a marker there.
Open the [b]map[/b] with M. Click a spot to place a marker there.
The [b]compass[/b] at the top shows your heading. For your first quest, gather stones, then follow bearing 180° (due south) to the river.
Knife equipped: butcher a carcass to get more meat.
You whistle: your horse is coming!
No tamed horse or dog to call.
Your horse is too far away to hear you.
Permanently delete %s's game? This cannot be undone.
Your horse and your dog come running!
%d animal(s) on the way: the pen is full (%d places).
No animal to herd or release.
The animal could not find the pen entrance.
Not enough room: a building is in the way.
Tame 3 animals in total (livestock, dog or horse).
Tame 8 animals in total: your ranch is taking shape.
The dog goes to guard the pen.
Night falls: %d animal(s) head into the pen.
Day breaks: %d animal(s) leave the pen.
shades you from the sun: thirst −20%
No pen yet: build one (Crafting tab).
Two dogs already guard this pen.
The pen is full: upgrade it for more room.
No upgradable building: build a shelter or a pen.
Your level: %d. Get within %d m of a building to upgrade it.
Canyons, mesas and dried-up rivers of the American West.
Red desert, bush and eucalyptus: extreme heat, very little water.
Tundra, boreal forest and snowy lakes, northern lights at night.
Change territory (current level: %d). Travelling loads the new map.
Your horse is in a pen or your dog is on guard: release them first (Ranch window).
You need a pickaxe in hand to mine iron.
You need %d iron ore and %d wood per ingot.
Craft a pickaxe, then mine 6 iron ore (rusty veins at the foot of the mesas).
Build a furnace and smelt 3 iron ingots.
